slides.prompt: Eight sentences are missing. How do we find them?
slides.hint: Two stories: the light bulb and fast travel.
slides.notes: 60-min Tue lesson 8 Sep 2026, sl_t3 17:50-18:50. Module pp.36-37 gapped text (P1P5, marks collected). Outcomes (teacher-kept): use the 4 checks on every gap; complete gaps 1-8 in books. 1M: noisy class, no roles or competitions; fingers vote + brief partner talk only.

slides.prompt: Alina wants to build a robot. What comes next?
options: She joins a robotics class and practises every week.
Her school has a new computer lab.
Many pupils watch robot videos online.
slides.answer: She joins a robotics class and practises every week.
slides.feedback: A stays with Alina and her plan. B is about the school. C is about other pupils.
slides.notes: Check 1 (topic). Fingers vote 1/2/3, then reveal. Module answers stay hidden for the marked bookwork.

slides.prompt: Mei brings home a small kitten. What comes next?
options: She feeds it milk in a warm box.
Kittens like string and soft toys.
Her brother walks to the market.
slides.answer: She feeds it milk in a warm box.
slides.feedback: She means Mei. It means the kitten. B and C lose the kitten.
slides.notes: Check 2 (who/what chain). Draw out: Mei to she, kitten to it.

slides.prompt: The hall was dark. Then the lamps lit up. What is missing?
options: The electrician had fixed the wires that morning.
Schools hold big events in the hall.
The lamps were made of glass.
slides.answer: The electrician had fixed the wires that morning.
slides.feedback: Only A joins both sides: the fault before, the light after.
slides.hint: Read before and after the gap.
slides.notes: Check 3 (both sides). The key habit: never read only one side of the gap.

slides.prompt: Razak hates traffic jams. What is his dream?
options: He imagines a machine that moves people instantly.
Buses in his town are old and slow.
Many people take the bus to work.
slides.answer: He imagines a machine that moves people instantly.
slides.feedback: Guess first: he wants instant travel. Only A gives that wish.
slides.notes: Check 4 (predict before options). 30-sec partner talk before voting. Teleportation flavour links to Module p.37 without revealing answers.

slides.prompt: Hakim studies old light bulbs. What comes next?
options: He draws one bulb in his notebook.
Edison was a famous American inventor.
The museum shows many kinds of lamps.
slides.answer: He draws one bulb in his notebook.
slides.feedback: A follows Hakim's work. B repeats a name but drops Hakim.
slides.hint: The same word can trick you.
slides.notes: Trap: keyword matching fails. Ask which sentence follows Hakim's action, not just a shared word. Invention flavour links to Module p.36.

slides.prompt: You see a gap. What do you check?
items: Topic: what is this part about?
People and things: who follows who?
Both sides: what must join up?
slides.notes: Rebuild the 4-check routine together. Leave visible during bookwork.

slides.answer: Gaps 1 to 4 use sentences A to D. Gaps 5 to 8 use sentences E to H.
slides.feedback: Two small sets. Never mix the two banks.
slides.notes: Light Bulb p.36 + Teleportation p.37 (LS 3.1.1/3.1.2). No module answers on slides; books carry the marked activity.

slides.task: Complete gaps 1 to 8 on pages 36 and 37. Use the 4 checks. Hand in your book for marks.
slides.frame: 1 Topic? 2 Who? 3 Both sides? 4 Predict, then choose.
slides.notes: Individual marked bookwork, about 20 min. P1P5, 8 marks. Collect books at the door.

slides.prompt: Tell your partner the 4 checks now.
slides.notes: Exit evidence, 2 min oral pair recall. Gaps in recall reopen next lesson.
